reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2, E3) only generically supports laser cladding for metallurgical bonding on steels (H13, 40Cr), not on TC4 titanium alloy. No evidence is provided for AlCoCrFeNiWx HEA synthesis, tungsten-induced strengthening mechanisms, or compatibility with TC4 substrates. The key premises about the specific coating material, its microstructural effects, and performance on TC4 are entirely unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Laser cladding can produce coatings with strong metallurgical bonding and low dilution on metallic substrates
AlCoCrFeNi-based HEAs can be doped with tungsten to induce lattice distortion and form reinforcing intermetallics
Tungsten doping in HEAs increases hardness and wear resistance via solid-solution and second-phase strengthening
A laser-clad HEA coating can be applied to TC4 without degrading the substrate's beneficial properties
The proposed coating will reduce friction and wear under high-contact-stress, high-temperature conditions
